title: Insecure Attachment, Oxytocinergic System and C-Tactile Fibers: An Integrative and Translational Pathophysiological Model of Fibromyalgia and Central Sensitivity Syndromes
authors: Gianluca Bruti; Paola Foggetti; Alessandro Rimessi
pain_condition_detail: fibromyalgia syndrome (FMS) and other central sensitivity syndromes (CSSs) such as migraine, irritable bowel syndrome, chronic low back pain, complex regional pain syndrome, post-herpetic neuralgia
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses the biopsychosocial model as an explanatory framework to integrate attachment system, C-tactile fibers, and oxytocinergic system dysfunction into a pathophysiological model of fibromyalgia and central sensitivity syndromes. It proposes a mechanistic pathway linking early attachment, CT fiber stimulation, and oxytocinergic programming to stress system dysregulation and central sensitization. The model is described narratively without formal operationalization of BPS domains.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes a mechanistic pathway: insecure attachment and early stress lead to dysfunction of C-tactile fibers and oxytocinergic system, which dysregulates the HPA axis and autonomic nervous system, resulting in central sensitization and chronic pain. This integrates biological (CT fibers, OS, HPA) and psychological (attachment, stress) domains mechanistically, but social factors are only descriptively linked.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper proposes a mechanistic bio-psych model but social factors are only mentioned, not integrated mechanistically
conceptual_tensions_2: Oxytocinergic system dysfunction and insecure attachment are described as 'two sides of the same coin', conflating biological and psychological constructs without clear distinction
conceptual_tensions_3: The paper uses the biopsychosocial label but the social domain is minimally developed, making the model effectively dyadic
conceptual_tensions_4: The proposed model is highly speculative and integrative but lacks empirical testing or operationalization of key constructs
additional_observations_1: The paper introduces a novel pathophysiological model integrating attachment theory, C-tactile fibers, and oxytocinergic system, but does not operationalize any of these constructs for measurement
additional_observations_2: The review is a narrative synthesis that cites empirical studies but does not conduct a systematic search or quality assessment
additional_observations_3: The term 'biopsychosocial' is used in the abstract and discussion but the paper's actual content is heavily weighted toward biological and psychological mechanisms, with social factors receiving only brief mentions
synthesis_note: This narrative review proposes an integrative pathophysiological model of fibromyalgia linking insecure attachment, C-tactile fiber dysfunction, and oxytocinergic system dysregulation to central sensitization. It uses the biopsychosocial label but operationalizes it as a dyadic bio-psych model with minimal social content. The model is mechanistic for bio-psych integration but social factors are only descriptively linked. The paper contributes a novel theoretical synthesis but does not empirically test or operationalize the model.
coding_rationale: Typology is pseudo_bps because BPS label is used but social domain is minimal. Triadic integration is partial: bio-psych is mechanistic, but social is only mentioned. Close call on bio-psych integration: the paper specifies pathways (CT fibers -> oxytocin -> HPA -> central sensitization), justifying 'mechanistic'.

title: Insecure Attachment, Oxytocinergic System and C-Tactile Fibers: An Integrative and Translational Pathophysiological Model of Fibromyalgia and Central Sensitivity Syndromes
authors: Gianluca Bruti; Paola Foggetti; Alessandro Rimessi
pain_condition_detail: Fibromyalgia syndrome and central sensitivity syndromes, with discussion of chronic widespread pain, migraine, IBS, low-back pain, post-herpetic neuralgia, CRPS, PTSD, and newborn pain.
context_note: No single country or healthcare system is specified; developmental and social context centers on parent-child dyads, caregiver participation, social support, and social context.
bps_function_set: conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; operational definition; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: It operationalizes BPS by turning the chronic-pain model into an attachment–CT–oxytocin neurodevelopmental mechanism: early caregiving/social adversity programs OS/CT systems and stress circuitry, producing emotional dysregulation, inflammation, central sensitization and pain; clinical care is framed as patient-centered and multidisciplinary.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes early social/caregiving adversity and insecure attachment to program OT/CT systems and stress-response circuitry, producing HPA/ANS dysregulation, inflammation, central sensitization, emotional dysregulation, threat perception, and chronic pain; OT/CT stimulation and caregiver/psychological interventions are framed as modifiable targets.
bps_model_variants_1: biopsychosocial model of chronic pain syndromes
emergent_labels_12: Fibromyalgia: Imbalance of Threat and Soothing Systems
conceptual_tensions_1: Small-fiber pathology in FMS is described as unclear in whether it is cause or consequence
conceptual_tensions_2: The discussion contrasts bottom-up nociceptive amplification with descending inhibitory dysfunction
conceptual_tensions_3: The threat/soothing model is questioned as possibly just another representation of ANS dysregulation
conceptual_tensions_4: Intranasal oxytocin for fibromyalgia pain is described as having negative results and limitations
conceptual_tensions_5: The paper states that whether attachment is key in CSSs and functional somatic disorders remains debated
additional_observations_1: The article is a narrative/translational pathophysiological model rather than an evidence synthesis
additional_observations_2: Social content is centered on attachment, caregiving, social support, dyads, and physician-patient relationships rather than work, income, culture, or policy
additional_observations_3: Clinical translation includes intranasal oxytocin, CT-fiber stimulation, psychoeducation, caregiver participation, and physician-patient relationship work
additional_observations_4: Developmental scope spans pregnancy, newborns, infancy, childhood, adolescence, and adulthood
additional_observations_5: The paper uses biomarkers such as HRV, cortisol, IENFD, oxytocin, and inflammatory markers as mechanistic evidence
additional_observations_6: No formal risk-of-bias or quality assessment is reported
synthesis_note: This narrative/translational paper operationalizes BPS as a neurodevelopmental attachment–CT–oxytocin model of fibromyalgia/CSSs. Biological stress, immune, neural and endocrine mechanisms are elaborated; psychological attachment/affect and social caregiving/social support are integrated, but social content is narrow.
coding_rationale: BPS is explicit but undefined. Biological and psychological content are elaborated; social is mentioned through attachment/caregiving. The triad is mechanistic but narrow.

title: Insecure Attachment, Oxytocinergic System and C-Tactile Fibers: An Integrative and Translational Pathophysiological Model of Fibromyalgia and Central Sensitivity Syndromes
authors: Gianluca Bruti; Paola Foggetti; Alessandro Rimessi
pain_condition_detail: fibromyalgia syndrome and central sensitivity syndromes
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; organizing principle
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses the biopsychosocial model as an organizing framework to structure its discussion of fibromyalgia pathophysiology, integrating biological (attachment system, CT fibers, oxytocin), psychological (stress response, threat system), and social (caregiving, bio-behavioral synchrony) factors without formally defining the model itself.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes a mechanistic triadic model where insecure attachment and early life stress dysregulate the attachment system and oxytocinergic system through altered bio-behavioral synchrony, leading to threat system hyperactivity and soothing system dysfunction, which together drive central sensitization and chronic pain.
bps_model_variants_1: biopsychosocial model of chronic pain syndromes
conceptual_tensions_1: The proposed 'Threat and Soothing Systems' model is criticized as not truly novel but rather a restatement of ANS dysregulation without incorporating recent findings on small fibers and immune mechanisms
conceptual_tensions_2: The paper uses the biopsychosocial label extensively but does not provide a formal definition of what the model means in this context
additional_observations_1: The paper presents a comprehensive integrative model linking early attachment experiences to chronic pain through neurobiological pathways involving CT fibers and oxytocin
additional_observations_2: The model emphasizes the developmental programming of stress response systems during the sensitive period of early life
additional_observations_3: The paper integrates findings from psychology, neuroscience, and social biology to explain fibromyalgia pathophysiology
synthesis_note: This paper provides a detailed integrative model of fibromyalgia pathophysiology that genuinely integrates biological, psychological, and social domains through mechanistic pathways. It uses the biopsychosocial model as an organizing framework but does not formally define it. The paper proposes that insecure attachment and early life stress dysregulate the attachment system and oxytocinergic system, leading to threat-soothing imbalance and central sensitization. While the integration is mechanistic, the paper acknowledges limitations in its model's novelty and comprehensiveness.
coding_rationale: The paper demonstrates true triadic integration with mechanistic pathways linking attachment, CT fibers, and oxytocin systems to stress response and central sensitization. The BPS model serves as an explanatory framework without formal definition. Integration is rated mechanistic based on explicit causal pathways proposed between all three domains.
